overview.text: William Shakespeare’s *A Midsummer Night’s Dream* is a comedy that brings together three worlds: the Athenian court preparing for Theseus and Hippolyta’s wedding, four young lovers whose affections tangle in a nearby wood, and workingmen rehearsing a play. In the forest, fairy king Oberon and queen Titania quarrel, while Puck’s flower magic confuses the lovers and leads Titania to fall for Bottom, whose head Puck transforms into an ass’s. The interwoven plots make love’s changeability comic and culminate in reconciled couples and the craftsmen’s performance of *Pyramus and Thisbe*. First printed in 1600, the play is distinctive for its play-within-a-play and its blend of romance, fairy magic, and farce.

key_facts.text: The four Athenian lovers are Hermia, Lysander, Helena, and Demetrius; the play ends with Hermia paired with Lysander and Helena with Demetrius.
Puck, also called Robin Goodfellow, serves Oberon; his tricks include using enchanted flower juice and giving Bottom an ass’s head.
Bottom and his fellow workers rehearse and perform the tragic story of Pyramus and Thisbe for the wedding celebration.
Oberon and Titania’s quarrel over a child is part of the fairy plot and prompts Oberon’s trick against Titania.
The play was first printed in 1600 as a quarto; the First Folio text appeared in 1623 and drew on the 1619 quarto.
